requirements_summary.purpose: Disaster planning and preparedness for wildfire risk assessment

data_sources.name: Satellite Vegetation Index Data
data_sources.justification: Essential for vegetation health and fuel load assessment. NDVI and biomass density data from 1984-present exceeds 10-year requirement. Daily to 16-day resolution enables seasonal analysis.

data_sources.name: Weather Station Climate Data
data_sources.justification: Critical for climate pattern analysis. Hourly temperature, humidity, wind, and precipitation data. LA County has dense weather station network. Historical data from 1950-present.

data_sources.name: US Drought Monitor
data_sources.justification: Provides drought severity classifications and soil moisture data. Weekly updates from 2000-present fully covers 10-year analysis period.

data_sources.name: EPA Air Quality System
data_sources.justification: Addresses air quality patterns requirement. Hourly PM2.5 and pollutant measurements. Historical data from 1980-present enables trend analysis and smoke impact assessment.

data_sources.name: Historical Wildfire Perimeters
data_sources.justification: Core dataset for 10-year historical pattern analysis. Provides fire boundaries, burn severity, frequency data. Essential for understanding LA County fire history and risk zones.

data_sources.name: Wildlife Habitat Database
data_sources.justification: Addresses wildlife habitat vulnerability requirement. Species distribution and habitat maps from 1990-present. Enables identification of at-risk wildlife areas in fire zones.

data_sources.name: Soil Erosion Risk Maps
data_sources.justification: Critical for post-fire erosion risk assessment. Provides soil types, erosion susceptibility, and topography data. Data from 2000-present covers analysis period.

data_sources.name: USGS Water Quality Data
data_sources.justification: Addresses water quality threats requirement. Stream flow and water chemistry data from 1900-present enables understanding of historical fire impacts on watersheds.

data_sources.name: Digital Elevation Models
data_sources.justification: Provides critical elevation, slope, and aspect data required for fire behavior modeling and erosion assessment. High-resolution terrain data essential for LA County's varied topography.

data_sources.name: National Land Cover Database
data_sources.justification: Provides land use and wildland-urban interface context. Critical for disaster planning in LA County where urban areas meet wildlands. Data from 1992-present supports temporal analysis.

analysis_models.name: Historical Fire Pattern Analysis
analysis_models.justification: First priority model to establish baseline understanding of 10-year fire patterns in LA County. Identifies fire frequency, seasonal trends, and return intervals. Essential foundation for all subsequent analyses.

analysis_models.name: Wildfire Risk Index Model
analysis_models.justification: Core risk assessment model combining vegetation, climate, and topography. Directly supports disaster planning purpose with risk scores and zones. All required data available from selected sources.

analysis_models.name: Vegetation Fuel Load Model
analysis_models.justification: Detailed assessment of combustible biomass and fuel conditions. Addresses vegetation health requirement and identifies fuel treatment priority areas for disaster preparedness.

analysis_models.name: Drought Severity Impact Model
analysis_models.justification: Analyzes drought contribution to fire risk. Directly addresses drought and soil moisture requirement. Provides ecosystem stress indicators valuable for disaster planning.

analysis_models.name: Fire-Related Air Quality Model
analysis_models.justification: Predicts smoke and air quality impacts from wildfires. Addresses air quality patterns requirement. Critical for public health components of disaster planning.

analysis_models.name: Wildlife Habitat Vulnerability Model
analysis_models.justification: Assesses wildlife habitat exposure to fire risk. Directly addresses wildlife habitat vulnerability requirement. Identifies priority conservation areas in high-risk zones.

analysis_models.name: Post-Fire Erosion Risk Model
analysis_models.justification: Predicts erosion and runoff risks after fire events. Addresses post-fire erosion risk requirement. Essential for understanding secondary disaster impacts.

analysis_models.name: Watershed Fire Impact Model
analysis_models.justification: Analyzes fire impacts on water quality and watersheds. Addresses water quality threats requirement. Critical for water supply protection planning.

analysis_models.name: Integrated Multi-Factor Fire Risk Model
analysis_models.justification: Comprehensive synthesis of all factors. Perfectly aligned with disaster planning purpose. Combines all previous analyses into holistic risk assessment with planning recommendations.

analysis_plan.primary_goal: Conduct comprehensive 10-year historical wildfire risk assessment for Los Angeles County to support disaster planning and preparedness, addressing vegetation/fuel dynamics, drought impacts, climate patterns, air quality, wildlife vulnerability, erosion risk, and water quality threats.
workflow_steps: Step 1: Data Acquisition (Est. 2-4 hours) - Download and preprocess all 10 data sources for LA County covering 2014-2024 period. Validate spatial and temporal coverage.

Step 2: Historical Pattern Analysis (Est. 1-2 hours) - Execute historical fire pattern model to identify 10-year trends, fire frequency, seasonal patterns, and return intervals. Output: Fire pattern report and trend maps.
Step 3: Core Risk Assessment (Est. 2-4 hours) - Run wildfire risk index model combining vegetation, climate, and topography. Output: Risk score maps and zone classifications.
Step 4: Vegetation and Drought Analysis (Est. 1.5-3 hours) - Execute fuel load and drought impact models in parallel. Outputs: Fuel load maps, treatment priorities, drought severity maps.
Step 5: Environmental Impact Analysis (Est. 4-7 hours) - Run air quality, wildlife habitat, erosion, and watershed models in parallel. Outputs: Impact zone maps for each factor.
Step 6: Integrated Synthesis (Est. 6-10 hours) - Execute comprehensive multi-factor model incorporating all previous outputs. Output: Integrated risk assessment and planning recommendations.
Step 7: Deliverable Generation (Est. 2-3 hours) - Compile reports, maps, executive summary, and planning recommendations for disaster management stakeholders.
analysis_plan.estimated_timeline: 18-33 hours total computational time (can parallelize Steps 4 and 5 to reduce to 20-28 hours wall-clock time)
analysis_plan.computational_requirements: high (comprehensive multi-model analysis with large spatial datasets)

resource_requirements.storage: 50-100 GB for raw and processed data
resource_requirements.compute: Multi-core processor recommended for parallel execution
resource_requirements.memory: 32+ GB RAM for large spatial datasets

deliverables: 10-Year Historical Fire Pattern Analysis Report with seasonal trends and frequency maps
Comprehensive Wildfire Risk Maps for LA County with risk scores (0-100) and zone classifications
Fuel Load Assessment with treatment priority areas and fuel moisture content maps
Drought Impact Analysis showing drought contribution to fire risk and temporal trends
Air Quality Impact Predictions with smoke dispersion patterns and health impact zones
Wildlife Habitat Vulnerability Maps identifying at-risk species and priority conservation areas
Post-Fire Erosion Susceptibility Maps with runoff risk zones and mitigation priorities
Water Quality Impact Assessment for critical watersheds with vulnerability zones
Integrated Multi-Hazard Risk Assessment synthesizing all factors
Planning Recommendations Report for disaster preparedness and emergency management
Executive Summary for decision-makers with key findings and actionable recommendations
GIS Data Package with all output layers in standard formats (Shapefile, GeoTIFF)

data_gaps: US Drought Monitor data begins in 2000, which limits pre-2000 drought trend analysis but fully covers the required 10-year period (2014-2024)
Wildlife Habitat Database updates annually, so most recent data may be 6-12 months old - will use latest available vintage
Some remote mountainous areas of LA County may have limited weather station coverage - satellite data will supplement ground observations
Land Cover Database updates every 2-3 years - will use most recent available (likely 2021 or 2023) with notation that land cover may have changed slightly
recommendations: Prioritize wildland-urban interface zones in LA County where fire risk intersects with populated areas for detailed analysis and planning
Consider seasonal analysis (summer/fall high-risk season vs. winter/spring) to support seasonal resource allocation and preparedness
After initial comprehensive analysis, identify top 5-10 highest risk zones for follow-up detailed studies and mitigation planning
Integrate results with LA County Fire Department emergency response plans, evacuation routes, and resource staging areas
Establish annual update schedule to track changing conditions as new fire events occur and environmental conditions evolve
Consider climate change scenarios for forward-looking risk projections beyond the historical analysis
Engage with local emergency management stakeholders to ensure deliverables align with existing disaster planning frameworks and decision-making processes
next_steps: Proceed to execution plan generation phase to create detailed technical specifications, data processing workflows, and model configuration parameters.
